title: Detached callbacks: schema rollback, partial emission SLAs, and streaming failover acceptance
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Purpose: define acceptance criteria and testable scenarios for detached (out-of-band) tool callbacks, partial/fragmented streaming emissions, schema rollback semantics, and SLA-driven failover behavior. This PRD supplements the streaming structured-output work by focusing on how the runtime and gateway should treat tool invocations that are executed separately from the main response stream (detached callbacks), how partial objects are committed and reparied, and what telemetry/guardrails are required for safe rollouts.

Context: Customers use function/tool-calling and streaming structured responses together. In several production scenarios (webhooks, external sidecars, managed tool gates) Redwood must support tool calls that may succeed or fail asynchronously relative to the primary streaming response. We need deterministic rules for schema pinning, partial emission commits, rollback, idempotency, and failover to fallback model variants or synthetic error frames.

Goals:
- Define unambiguous commit/rollback semantics for partial/fragmented objects emitted during a stream when a detached callback is involved.
- Ensure idempotent tool invocation patterns with clear retry/backoff rules and observable correlation keys.
- Surface precise error classifications to consumers (transient/retryable vs irrecoverable vs degraded-result) so applications can react programmatically.
- Provide test cases and rollout steps to validate behavior on hosted and Dedicated deployments.

Non-goals:
- Adding a new wire protocol; this work uses existing framed-stream envelope semantics.
- Redesign of the function gateway plumbing (engineering will adapt current gateway hooks to satisfy criteria).
assumptions: Streaming response envelope supports typed frames and checkpoint markers
Tool gateway and main runtime can exchange correlation IDs and commit tokens
Clients consuming streams understand envelope-level error frames and can apply simple backoff logic
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Detached callback correlation: Every detached tool invocation MUST include a correlation_id that matches the stream session_id or a parent_emit_token. The runtime must emit a correlation frame in-stream immediately after scheduling the detached call.

AC-2: Commit token handshake: When a partial object is emitted over the stream that depends on a detached callback (for example, an attachment URL or external metadata), the stream MUST include an optimistic commit_token. The detached callback must return an explicit commit_ack(token) or commit_reject(token, reason). The runtime accepts the final object only after commit_ack or after commit_timeout expiry with documented fallback behavior.

AC-3: Commit timeout and soft degrade: If commit_ack is not received within configurable commit_timeout (default: 12s for hosted), the runtime MUST emit a soft-degrade frame in-stream with classification: RETRYABLE_TEMPORARY or SOFT_MISSING_EXTERNAL. Clients must be able to detect soft-degrade and present partial content with a clear UX affordance. Default behavior: switch to fallback field value provided in original schema or mark field as null with provenance metadata.

AC-4: Rollback semantics: If commit_reject is received, the runtime MUST emit a rollback frame that indicates which object fragments must be considered invalid. Any downstream tooling (caches, indexers) receiving the prior partial fragment must ignore or delete the data within 5s of rollback emission. Rollback MUST be idempotent and reference the original commit_token.

AC-5: Idempotency and retry: Detached callbacks must accept an idempotency_key header. Retries from the gateway MUST be limited by retry_policy: exponential backoff, max_attempts=3, and client-visible retry_count shown in telemetry. Duplicate successful commits MUST not produce duplicate side-effects; gateway should prefer at-least-once submit but deduplicate using idempotency_key.

AC-6: Error taxonomy mapping: The runtime and gateway MUST classify detached-callback failures into one of: TRANSIENT_RETRYABLE, AUTH_FAILURE, VALIDATION_FAILURE, UPSTREAM_RATE_LIMIT, or PERMANENT. These classifications must be emitted as named fields in an error frame and recorded in per-request telemetry with standardized error codes (e.g., DC_01..DC_10).

AC-7: Observable lineage and replay: For any request that emits detached callbacks, the request trace MUST include a lineage list (array of correlation_ids and commit_tokens) accessible via the Console trace view and the /requests API. Operators must be able to replay or re-run detached callbacks from Console and mark replays as 'operator-initiated' with audit metadata.

AC-8: Backpressure and cancellation: If downstream consumer cancels the stream (client disconnect), the runtime MUST cancel any pending detached callbacks within cancel_grace_period (default 5s) unless commit_timeout is already in flight and the policy for completion_on_disconnect is set to true for the customer. Cancellation events must emit a CANCEL frame that includes reason and pending_commit_tokens.

AC-9: Test harness: The PRD must include a simulation harness capable of injecting: delayed commit_acks, commit_rejects, rate limit responses, intermittent auth failures, and client disconnects. The harness must run in CI and assert expected frames and Console telemetry for 95% of randomized trials.

AC-10: Cross-environment parity: Behavior must be identical across hosted and Dedicated modes with configuration knobs surfaced in Console (commit_timeout, cancel_grace_period, completion_on_disconnect). Private deployments will get the same defaults but can override via config; acceptance includes docs and a migration note for on-prem ops teams.
test_cases: TC-1: Happy path: Stream emits partial object with commit_token -> detached callback returns commit_ack within 200ms -> final commit frame emitted and telemetry shows event sequence [emit, correlate, ack, commit]

TC-2: Late ack: commit_ack arrives after commit_timeout -> runtime must have already emitted soft-degrade; upon late ack runtime should emit commit_resolve frame and record a late_ack metric. Client-visible state stays consistent (shows degraded then resolved).
TC-3: Reject path: detached callback returns commit_reject -> runtime emits rollback frame and downstream storage receives delete_event; telemetry includes DC_03 VALIDATION_FAILURE code.
TC-4: Retry dedupe: gateway retries a detached callback twice with same idempotency_key -> side-effect executed once; telemetry shows retry_count=2 and dedupe_success=true.

TC-5: Cancel on disconnect: client disconnects after emission but before commit_ack -> runtime cancels call after cancel_grace_period and emits CANCEL frame; console shows pending_commit_tokens list and cancel outcome.

TC-6: Rate-limit spike: detached gateway receives 429 -> classified as UPSTREAM_RATE_LIMIT, runtime emits soft-degrade with suggested_retry_after and increments circuit_breaker counter; fallback content is used.

TC-7: Observability: run end-to-end with Console trace: the lineage array must contain at least three events and every detached callback must have telemetry keys correlation_id, idempotency_key, start_time, end_time, outcome_code.
qa_checklist: Unit tests for commit token generation and validation
Integration test with detached gateway simulator (inject faults)
End-to-end smoke on hosted and dedicated staging with Console trace verification
Docs: developer guide for using correlation_id and idempotency_key
Security review for detached callback auth patterns and token propagation
Add observability dashboards: detached-callback-latency, commit-timeouts, late-acks, rollback-rate
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary 5%): runtime-1.22 canary with detached-callback enabled for internal orgs only. Observe telemetry for 48h.
Phase 2 (beta 25%): enable for public customers who opt in; run full test harness; collect customer feedback via Solutions SEs.
Phase 3 (GA): enable by default with docs and SDK examples; mark runtime-1.22 as supported for Dedicated and Hosted.
Rollback criteria: conversion failure rate to soft-degrade > 3% above baseline for 24h or rollback events causing data loss in >1 customer (investigate and rollback).
